statusText:
The CME weekend halt frames this entire assessment. Nothing has quoted NQ since the weekly close at 21:00 UTC on Friday 14 August, and nothing will until the Sunday reopen near 22:00 UTC on 16 August - roughly five hours past the end of this 24-hour horizon. Tail is 11% (low), the action is EA_ON and the status is green, because a pathological one-way price path cannot form while no venue is quoting.

What changed this hour is tone, not price. The constructive Hormuz thread that carried into Friday - Iran and Oman agreeing the coordinates of a safe two-way shipping corridor - was partly walked back today. Bloomberg reports the two sides have still not agreed on actually reopening the strait despite earlier optimism, while Iran's deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi said the waterway blockade will continue until the United States accepts defeat, and the IRGC attached conditions including an end to the US naval blockade and compensation for war damages. President Trump, for his part, has threatened to declare Hormuz US territory. Ship attacks in the strait continue to mount and transit volumes remain a fraction of pre-conflict norms.

That is why Stress rises to 60% (elevated) rather than decaying into the weekend. Stress here is not a claim about the next hour - it is the width of the distribution that will be repriced in a single print at the Sunday reopen. Tail stays low because the mechanism Tail measures, repeated extension after failed pullbacks, requires a quoting market and there is none.
recommendation:
Action is EA_ON with a green status, derived from the current Tail of 11% alone. No venue quotes NQ or NAS100 anywhere inside the 24-hour horizon and no scheduled US macro release falls within it, so there is no evidential basis for a directional or event-driven block in this window. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always.

The operative checkpoint sits just beyond the horizon: the CME reopen near 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, where any weekend Hormuz development gets repriced in one gap rather than through a tradable path. The danger window is anchored to that instant. Treat the reopen as the point at which observed structure becomes scoreable again; nothing before it changes the picture.

This is general market-risk commentary for a public dashboard, not personalised financial advice and not a trade instruction.
headline: Tehran hardens its Hormuz line - Gharibabadi says the blockade holds until the US accepts defeat and Bloomberg reports no reopening deal despite earlier optimism - Stress up to 60%, Tail 11% with CME shut, action EA_ON.
body:
PRICE PATH (observed, necessarily stale). No venue has quoted NQ since the CME weekly close at 21:00 UTC on Friday 14 August, and none will until the Sunday reopen near 22:00 UTC on 16 August. The last live structure, re-verified this hour directly from the quote page, is benign: September E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures show a last print of 30,141.75, -46.75 points or -0.15% against a previous close of 30,188.50, on 397,964 contracts, opening at 30,210.75 and settling inside a 30,028.50-30,283.00 band roughly 255 points or 0.84% wide, with the close pinned to neither extreme. NQ sits about 2.7% below its 52-week high of 30,975.50 against a 52-week low of 22,961.50. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 30,046.14, -38.36 points or -0.13%, opening at 30,167.13 inside a 29,934.66-30,179.82 range, about 2.3% below its 52-week high of 30,762.20. A two-way intraday range with a mid-range settle, several percent off the highs, is the opposite of the persistent directional efficiency, shallow pullbacks, repeated extension and pinning near extremes that the Tail definition requires. Directional efficiency here is not merely low - it is unmeasurable, because nothing has traded for more than twenty-one hours.

CROSS-ASSET (observed, Friday close, all re-read directly this hour). The split in the evidence is the central fact of this assessment. Equity volatility is calm to the point of complacency: VIX closed at 14.25, -0.38 or -2.60%, inside a 14.18-14.72 range and less than a point above its 13.38 annual low, against a 35.30 annual high. Rates are the opposite: the US 10-year yield closed at 4.696%, +5.5 basis points, in a 4.625-4.700% range and within five basis points of its 4.747% 52-week high; the 2-year closed at 4.171%, +3.1 basis points, in a 4.098-4.178% band against a 3.365-4.370% annual range. The curve is roughly +52 basis points 2s10s with the long end doing the work - a bear-steepening impulse that is a live headwind for long-duration Nasdaq megacap multiples if it extends. Energy is the third leg and it is hot: WTI at $82.40, +$1.15 or +1.42% on the day, up roughly 5% on the week and about 33% year-on-year; Brent at $88.52, +$1.45 or +1.67%, up about 34% year-on-year. Complacent equity vol sitting on top of a bid energy complex and yields at the top of their annual range is the textbook definition of a mixed, conflicting regime - and per the risk contract, conflicting signals raise Stress rather than Tail.

GEOPOLITICS (new this hour, and the reason Stress rises). The Hormuz thread deteriorated in tone over the last hour relative to the constructive reading that carried into Friday. Bloomberg reports that Iran and Oman have yet to reach an agreement on reopening the strait despite earlier optimism that a deal was close, even as work on a shipping map continues, and that ship attacks are mounting while the US readies new economic measures. Iran's deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi said the waterway blockade will continue until the United States accepts defeat, and restated that Hormuz has been, is and will remain Iranian and will open only under Iran's command. The IRGC has attached conditions to any reopening including an end to the US naval blockade, withdrawal of forces, a permanent end to the war and compensation for war damages, and Iran's national security chief issued a further list of demands today. President Trump has threatened to declare Hormuz US territory 'pretty soon' and the US says it can maintain the blockade indefinitely. Transit volumes remain a small fraction of normal - Bloomberg puts the past seven days at roughly 17% of the pre-conflict average. This is a negotiation moving sideways under active kinetic pressure, which widens the weekend headline distribution in both directions.

CATALYSTS AND CALENDAR. Nothing scheduled falls inside the 24-hour horizon; the entire window is a weekend halt. The next seven days, verified from the calendar this hour, begin quietly - Empire State and NAHB on Monday 17 August - then thicken: Housing Starts and Building Permits plus Industrial Production on Tuesday 18 August, EIA crude stocks and the FOMC Minutes from the 28-29 July meeting on Wednesday 19 August, Jobless Claims and the Philadelphia Fed index on Thursday 20 August, and the S&P Global flash PMIs on Friday 21 August. The Jackson Hole symposium falls on 27-29 August, outside this seven-day window, so it is excluded. The FOMC Minutes on Wednesday are the week's single largest scheduled repricing risk given where the long end already sits.

SCORING. Tail 11% (low): no quoting venue for the whole horizon, and the last observed path was two-way with a mid-range settle - none of the amplifier conditions the contract requires for 25%+ are present or even observable. Stress 60% (elevated): a hardened Hormuz negotiation, a bid energy complex, the 10-year within five basis points of its annual high, and a genuine gap risk waiting at the Sunday reopen. Confidence 63% (solid): price, volatility, rates, energy and the seven-day calendar were all read directly from primary sources this hour, but there is no live price path to score and the geopolitical evidence is internally conflicting, which caps this below the high band. Dominant mode is mixed. Action EA_ON, status green, from Tail alone.

This is general market-risk analysis for a public dashboard. It is not personalised financial advice and contains no trade instruction.

lookbackSummary: Across the trailing 24 clock-hours Tail never left the low band, running 2-11%, so the action was EA_ON and the status green in every available slot. Tail held 7-9% through the back half of Friday's US cash session - where the data landed and produced two-way volatility and rotation rather than directional efficiency - then printed 6% into the 21:00 UTC weekly close and settled at 10-11% across the weekend halt, where no path can form. Stress traced the more informative line: it rose steadily from the low-40s late Friday to 51% by 09:00 UTC Saturday and on to 58% at 16:00 UTC as the Hormuz sequence and the energy bid accumulated, easing one point to 57% at 17:25 UTC on the corridor-coordinates headline before today's harder line from Tehran reversed that. Confidence sat in the 45-62% range, improving through Saturday as each hour re-verified the Friday-close evidence base from primary sources. One slot in the window is unavailable. No past opinion has been rewritten.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt: it runs from 18:00 UTC on Saturday 15 August to 17:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, ending roughly five hours before the reopen near 22:00 UTC that day, so neither a scheduled US macro release nor a tradable price path falls within it. Tail is projected flat at 11% through Saturday evening and the overnight, stepping to 12% from 06:00 UTC and 13% into Sunday afternoon - conditional gap risk building toward a reopen that lands outside the window, not observed structure. Every slot therefore stays EA_ON and green. Stress eases marginally to 58% in the deepest part of the news vacuum, then rebuilds to 63% by the end of the horizon as the reopen approaches and unresolved Hormuz headline risk accumulates with no venue able to price it. Confidence decays from 63% to 55% by design, because the Friday-close evidence base ages the whole way through with nothing able to refresh it. The single checkpoint that matters is the Sunday reopen, and the danger window is anchored there.
